data.why: The repo already bundles outputs/predictions/all_predictions.csv(.gz), the 98,394-row precomputed yield lookup table the app loads at startup, so nothing needs to be copied in; batch_crosses.csv is a small upload file (real Female/Male/Location combos plus one unknown cross) for the Batch Predict tab's file_uploader.

goals: Predict the yield of a specific hybrid cross (female x male parent) at a chosen US field location
Find the best-performing location for a given hybrid cross
Find the top-yielding crosses at a chosen location
Compare 2-4 hybrids side by side across yield, percentile rank and stability
Assess genotype x environment (G x E) stability of hybrids to identify wide-adapted vs location-specific crosses
Batch-predict yields for a list of crosses uploaded as CSV and export a PDF/CSV report of results

review.summary: The tree fits the README's purpose well: choosing crosses and test sites from predicted yield and G×E stability before field trials. Its tasks cover every main tab, and the screens I sampled mostly show exactly the values cited. It needs a few fixes before filing: break up the oversized f1 and t2, stop mirroring the tab bar in the phases, fix the t3 citation and the batch-failure explanation, and file the replay's missing screens.
